title: Chora Church (Kariye), Istanbul
summary: The Chora church in Istanbul was funded in the early 14th century by Theodore Metochites, who paid for its restoration, mosaics, frescoes and a side chapel. It was made a mosque before 1511, a museum in 1945, and reopened for worship on 6 May 2024 after restoration.

uncertainty.note: Turkish Archaeological News gives 1310–1317 for the decoration and 1315–1321 for the additions; the Istanbul museum page says only the 14th century. The building has older phases. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: The decoration sponsored by Theodore Metochites between 1310 and 1321

when.display: Current church and mosaics c. 1310–1321; in use today

where.modern_name: Kariye Mosque (Chora Church), Fatih, Istanbul, Turkey
where.historical_name: Chora monastery church, Constantinople, Byzantine Empire

importance.justification: The Istanbul museum directorate presents the building with its 14th-century mosaics and frescoes as a monument that served as church, mosque and museum.

reviewer_note: No model: pages opened give no height; Turkish Archaeological News gives only a total area of about 742.5 m2 and dome diameters. The 1310 start is the Metochites decoration date from one non-institutional page; the museum page says only 14th century.
